concepts.def: Policies that shield domestic industry from imports.
Numerical limit on imports of a good.
Government payment to lower production costs.
Trade without tariffs or other barriers.
Country produces at lower opportunity cost.
Balance of trade plus net income/transfers.

walkthroughs.body_html: Tariffs raise import prices, helping domestic firms but hurting consumers. Quotas cap imports. Subsidies cut domestic costs. Trade-off: protect jobs vs higher prices and possible retaliation (e.g. US-China tariff war 2018).

Winners: consumers (cheap goods), MNCs, developing economies that industrialise. Losers: workers in declining industries, the environment, sometimes culture. Top-band answers weigh both sides and pick context (UK textiles, Chinese factory workers).

A weak £ initially worsens trade balance (J-curve) because import costs jump immediately but export volumes adjust slowly. Over 1–2 years, exports rise and the balance improves. Mention the J-curve for top marks.
